root_cause.text: In airoha_qdma_rx_process(), the RX error path incorrectly assumed non-linear RX page_pool fragments were attached to q->skb, so when an error occurred on subsequent fragments before linkage, page_pool pages were not returned and leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path,” and the patch changes the cleanup logic to call page_pool_put_full_page() unconditionally instead of only in the q->skb == NULL case.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In airoha_qdma_rx_process(), the RX error path incorrectly assumed non-linear RX page_pool fragments were attached to q->skb, so when an error occurred on subsequent fragments before linkage, page_pool pages were not returned and leaked.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that “the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path,” and the patch changes the cleanup logic to call page_pool_put_full_page() unconditionally instead of only in the q->skb == NULL case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always return the RX page to the page pool after processing, even when an skb was present, to avoid losing page recycling.
intent_record.what: The conditional branch around page_pool_put_full_page() was removed so that after freeing q->skb when present and clearing q->skb, the function now always calls page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true) instead of only calling it in the else case when q->skb was absent.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the page backing the receive buffer is now always returned to the page pool regardless of whether q->skb existed, preventing the page from being skipped and potentially leaked or left unrecycled when an skb had been attached.

grouping_result.intent: Always return the RX page to the page pool after processing, even when an skb was present, to avoid losing page recycling.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses leaked RX page_pool pages on error/processing paths by ensuring the RX page is always returned to the page pool, matching the root cause of pages not being recycled when fragments were not attached to q->skb.

candidates.rationale: This conditional split is the core faulty assumption: when an skb existed, the code assumed the RX page had been attached to it, so it skipped returning the page to the page pool on the error path, causing leaks for unlinked subsequent fragments.

This page return happened only in the else branch, meaning pages were recycled only when no skb was present. That directly caused leaked page_pool pages when errors occurred with q->skb already set but the current fragment not yet linked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional embodies the incorrect assumption that when q->skb exists, the current non-linear RX page_pool fragment has already been attached to it. On the RX error path, that assumption prevented unconditional recycling of the current page, so subsequent fragments that errored before linkage were leaked.

This page_pool return was only executed in the else branch when no skb was present. Because it was not reached when q->skb was already set, the current fragment page was not returned on error if it had not yet been linked, directly causing the page leak.

commit d6d2b0e1538d5c381ec0ca95afaf772c096ea5dc
Author: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu May 15 08:33:06 2025 +0200

    net: airoha: Fix page recycling in airoha_qdma_rx_process()
    
    Do not recycle the page twice in airoha_qdma_rx_process routine in case
    of error. Just run dev_kfree_skb() if the skb has been allocated and marked
    for recycling. Run page_pool_put_full_page() directly if the skb has not
    been allocated yet.
    Moreover, rely on DMA address from q
bic_trace_step.reason:
The diff shows the exact RX error-path logic in `airoha_qdma_rx_process()` and is sufficient to determine the issue. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause would be an unconditional `page_pool_put_full_page()` on error even when `q->skb` already exists, because in that case the fragment may already be owned by the skb or the skb free path should handle recycling. In this commit, the `free_frag:` block has been changed from unconditional cleanup:

`page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true);`
`dev_kfree_skb(q->skb);`
`q->skb = NULL;`

to conditional handling:

`if (q->skb) {`
`    dev_kfree_skb(q->skb);`
`    q->skb = NULL;`
`} else {`
`    page_pool_put_full_page(q->page_pool, page, true);`
`}`

This is the fix: when an skb already exists, the code no longer directly recycles the page and instead only frees the skb; when no skb exists yet, it returns the page directly to the page pool. That matches the commit message and prevents the erroneous recycling/leak behavior in the error path. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.

The vulnerable root cause was that the error path always recycled the current page with `page_pool_put_full_page(...)` and then also freed `q->skb`, incorrectly assuming the fragment was already attached to `q->skb`.
